correctness.rationale: The object is explicitly defined as the induced linear-forest complex of the 18-vertex 36-edge categorical product. The verifier checks all 262144 subsets by two independent predicates and finds 49743 faces. Two opposite-order, fully acyclic Morse matchings each have 24826 pairs and critical cells of dimensions 6/7/8/9 in ranks 16/33/36/6, with every one of 322092 incidences checked. Signed integer Morse elimination yields a degree-seven 16-by-33 differential having 16 private unit columns (hence a determinant +/-1 minor), and literally zero degree-eight and degree-nine differentials. This establishes \(\widetilde H_7\cong\mathbb Z^{17}\), \(\widetilde H_8\cong\mathbb Z^{36}\), \(\widetilde H_9\cong\mathbb Z^6\) and no other integral groups, including absence of torsion. Direct independent mod-two ranks of original simplicial boundaries are 5216/7570/6326/2360/246 for degrees 5..9. One ordinary 0-cell and no 1..5-cells imply 5-connectivity; H~6=0 and Hurewicz give 6-connectivity. This verifies the precise finite statement, not the unproved full homotopy type.

originality.rationale: The primary source arXiv:2307.13271, Question 44, asks about positive forest-filtration levels of triple categorical products, but its Theorem 42 is two-factor only and Corollary 43 assumes two binary factors. The closest direct categorical triple-product paper arXiv:2307.12401 computes only the independence complex F0, while arXiv:2307.14321 studies lexicographic rather than categorical products. A recoverable earlier F1 computation of exactly this graph establishes a different filtration stage and does not imply F2 homology. The isomorphic product notation C6 x K3 was explicitly compared. Comparisons of published mathematical records, web literature and prior first-stage mathematical statements found no dominating theorem or exact table that implies the 17/36/6 integral ranks. Unindexed literature remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An independently published but unindexed degree-two calculation for the isomorphic C6 x K3 graph might exist.
This finite integral homology result does not determine unstable attaching maps or the complete homotopy type.

value.rationale: The original forest-filtration article poses Question 44 about positive-level triple products. The balanced nonbinary K2 x K3 x K3 is a small canonical case; determining its complete F2 integral homology at a genuinely higher filtration stage addresses this motivation directly. Unlike its known F1 sphere wedge, the F2 complex has free homology in three consecutive degrees 7/8/9 and 6-connectivity, supplying structural information not predictable from face counts or the previous level. The calculation gives all integral ranks and torsion exclusion rather than an arbitrary partial enumeration; it is a useful exact test case, although no general formula or complete homotopy splitting is claimed.
